_note: Bill of materials for the farm monitor of chapters 1-9. Every unit price is an ASSUMPTION: a typical single-unit retail price in USD in 2026, rounded, not a quotation; the `source` field says so per line. The brief's budget line is `budget_usd` per class. The fan and the valve are the farm's own loads; the node switches them, so only a contactor allowance appears here.

classes.name: greenhouse node
classes.budget_from: brief B5: under 150 USD of hardware per greenhouse

parts.part: ESP32-WROOM-32 DevKit (4 MB flash, two app slots for OTA)
parts.why: six tasks on FreeRTOS (ch4), Wi-Fi (ch6), two OTA slots (ch9)
±0.5 °C requirement (ch1); own I2C bus so the display never delays a reading (ch4)
fan contactor coil and valve; active-high so a pull-down means off (N4)

parts.part: 10 kΩ pull-down resistors on the relay driver pins
parts.why: the relay is off before the first instruction (N4, ch4 boot order)

parts.part: heartbeat gate: retriggerable monostable (CD4538) + second relay in series with the valve
parts.why: the valve closes when the safety task stops pulsing: a hung MCU or a declared fault (ch5 layer 3)

parts.part: hardware max-on timer for the valve (second monostable, 30 min)
parts.why: a shorted valve relay cannot flood for longer than 30 min without the firmware re-arming the timer (ch5 layer 4, N1 valve row)

parts.part: contactor sized to the fan (electrician's part, allowance)
parts.why: the relay module switches a coil, never the fan's current (poultry HARDWARE.md says the same)
N1's local response and N2's error alarm do not depend on the network
the display computation is on the device (ch2 R4)
history outbox for N6 (2 h at 15 s is 480 readings) and the log a person pulls once (ch9)

parts.part: 5 V 2 A supply with a fused IEC inlet
parts.why: mains at the greenhouse (brief B4); the fuse is the first layer of the energy path (ch5)
a greenhouse is wet; the relays and the mains side stay behind a lid
the label carries the device id and the per-unit hotspot password (ch7 H5)

classes.name: plot node
classes.budget_from: no line in the brief; the greenhouse budget is the yardstick

parts.part: ESP32 + SX1276 LoRa board with 868 MHz antenna
parts.why: 200 m is out of Wi-Fi reach (ch6 X1); LoRaWAN class A at SF8
soil moisture in the plot (brief B1); a resistive probe corrodes in a season
tank level in the plot (brief B1)

parts.part: 18650 cell 2 000 mAh with holder and protection
parts.why: ch6's battery budget: 1.16 mAh/day at SF8, about 3.3 years on 0.7 of the nameplate
outdoors all year
label as above

classes.name: LoRaWAN gateway (one per farm, at greenhouse 1)
classes.budget_from: no line in the brief; it is the plot node's cost of reach (ch6)

parts.part: 8-channel indoor LoRaWAN gateway with Wi-Fi backhaul
parts.why: translates the plot node's 11-byte frames into chapter 3's records and forwards them over the farm Wi-Fi (ch2, ch6)
200 m to the plot through a greenhouse wall
mains at greenhouse 1; its power supply is on the never-list (ch6 hand-over 5)

farm._note: The brief's farm: two greenhouse nodes, one plot node, one gateway; the farm's own Wi-Fi router is already there (brief B4).

operations_usd_per_hour.source: assumption: what an hour of a part-time operator costs the cooperative; the hours themselves come from chapter 8's fleet.json
